newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada able to handle most tough, damp grain - CWB.
newsitem.headline: Canada able to handle most tough, damp grain - CWB.

text.p: Canadian grain elevators should be able to dry "a large portion" of tough and damp grain but low grade milling wheat may be difficult to dry, the Canadian Wheat Board said on Thursday.
Two-thirds of low grade No3 Canada Western Red Spring milling wheat is tough and damp, the CWB said.
The western Prairie harvest was hampered by cold, wet conditions in October as well as early snowfall.
The elevator system cannot handle all of the tough grain stored on farms due to limited port drying capabilities, CWB western manager of grain operations, Stan Sichewski said.

Delivery of tough or damp No3 CWRS wheat may be restricted by its large volume. Estimates of tonnage or the percentage of the overall wheat crop that would be considered tough or damp were not available.
A C$7 a tonne discount will be applied to the 1996/97 (Aug/July) CWB initial payment for the cost of drying tough wheat at terminal elevators while the actual cost is C$9.75 a tonne, the CWB said.
A C$14.50 a tonne discount will be applied to the initial payment for drying damp wheat while the real cost is C$12.65.
There is also the cost of shrinkage, the loss of weight after drying, the CWB added.
Additional costs will be shown as deductions from the CWB final payment.
